study type: Secondary analysis of a cross-sectional study, designed as an observational analytical case-control study
exposure: acetaminophen consumption (at least once a month)
exposure to exhaust fumes during the day
cohort: The study included 5978 subjects from six cities in Colombia, comprising two subpopulations: children and adolescents (aged 1-17 years) and adults (aged 18-59 years).
finding: The study found that different cultural, environmental, and family factors, such as family history of allergic diseases, acetaminophen consumption, presence of pets, and environmental smoke/fume exposure, are associated with asthma symptoms in both child/adolescent and adult populations.
